messages:
maya: FYI — ran a concurrency/throughput sweep for mha-3b (int8) on dedicated-us-west yesterday. p95 latency doubles around concurrency=32 compared to float baseline. Posting minimal logs and commands below for triage.

perf-bot: perf-sweep finished: https://perf.redwood/experiments/1864127890 :bar_chart: results uploaded (partial traces)

liam: can you paste the exact eval_runner invocation you used?

maya: Sure — command I used:```
# run sweep
python eval_runner.py --model mha-3b-int8 --pool dedicated-us-west --concurrency 1,4,8,16,32,64 --qps 0 --duration 300 --batch-ms 10
```

igor: quick snippet from runner logs around the p95 jump:```
[2026-03-18T11:12:05.123Z] INFO batch_size=1 processing_time_ms=12.1 kv_cache_hit=false
[2026-03-18T11:12:05.134Z] INFO batch_size=8 processing_time_ms=9.3 kv_cache_hit=true
[2026-03-18T11:12:35.999Z] WARN kv_cache_miss_ratio=0.46 run_id=1864127890 stage=decode
[2026-03-18T11:13:00.001Z] INFO batch_size=4 processing_time_ms=21.8 kv_cache_hit=false
```

priya: interesting — KV cache miss ratio spikes. int8 path sometimes touches a different memory layout and can cause more cache churn. Did you run with the same kernel selection flags as the float baseline?

jon: also FYI earlier CI run had artifact upload errors so the dashboard may be missing full server-side traces for a subset of the sweep. saw a 413 on artifact upload.

dev-ci-bot: upload failed: HTTP 413 Payload Too Large POST /artifacts/upload/1864127890/trace.tar.gz (trace size=124MB)

maya: ack. so two angles: (1) harness is currently reporting client-side end-to-end p95, our SLOs use server-side model_exec_time. (2) we might be generating many tiny batches due to batch-ms=10 which could interact poorly with int8 kernel warmup/cache behavior.

liam: good catch on metric definition mismatch. client-side includes network + queuing. under high concurrency that extra time can inflate p95. do we have server-side model_exec_time in the trace?

maya: only partial traces uploaded. grep shows some model_exec_time events in trace.json but not for every run. quick grep:```
jq '.events[] | select(.name=="model_exec_time") | .duration_ns' trace.json | wc -l
# returns 23 (we had 48 samples)
```

tara: we should make the harness prefer server-side metrics when available and fall back to client timing. small PR candidate: change metric extraction to prefer 'model_exec_time' tag.

jon: another likely contributor: quant kernel selection fallback. On older drivers the int8 fused kernels sometimes fallback to slower fp16 kernels or to less-optimized matmul. Check the runner env var and driver version. run:```
ssh runner-host-01 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv'
```

igor: also noticed tokenization mismatch in the cost calc — the run used a different tokenizer path (byte-bpe) and that inflated tokens-per-char. cost-per-token jumped accordingly in the report. snippet:```
input: "Hello world"
tokens: ["▁Hello", "▁world"]  # looks like sentencepiece vs expected byte-bpe
```

priya: quant kernels + batching + tokenization differences is a nasty 3-way interaction. suggestion: rerun a scoped sweep with: (A) batch_ms=30, (B) explicit ENV USE_INT8_KERNELS=1, (C) forced tokenizer path to canonical tokenizer, and (D) smaller trace files (rotate) so uploads don't hit 413.

perf-bot: dashboard note: panel 'mha-3b-int8 latency p95' missing tag run_id for recent sweeps due to truncated artifact metadata. patch queued to add run_id fallback to query.

jon: CI side — the artifact uploader should fallback to S3 multipart for >50MB traces. dev-ci-bot can you enable multipart for this bucket?

dev-ci-bot: enabling multipart upload for bucket redwood-perf-traces (will retry next upload)

liam: small grep to compute server-side mean model_exec_time quickly:```
jq '.events[] | select(.name=="model_exec_time") | .duration_ns' trace.json | awk '{sum+=$1;count++}END{print (count?sum/count:0)/1e6 " ms"}'
```

maya: I'll kick off the scoped rerun with the 4 adjustments now (batch_ms=30, USE_INT8_KERNELS=1, tokenizer forced, multipart upload enabled). ETA ~3h. I'll post new traces + p95 comparison when done.

igor: if p95 still high we should capture kernel selection logs from the runtime (enable RUNTIME_DEBUG=1) and grab a nvprof/cupti sample on a single host.

tara: I'll open a tiny PR to prefer server-side metrics and to label runs with run_id before artifact upload to avoid dashboard gaps.

maya: thanks all — ping me if you want to pair on the trace parsing. :eyes:

liam: :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: schedule nightly regression that compares int8 vs fp16 p95/cost-per-token at 3 concurrency points (8/32/64) — will surface deltas in the weekly report.

maya: closing loop once rerun finishes.
